system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: ODYSSEY OUTCOMES NCT01663402 - ODYSSEY Outcomes: Evaluation of Cardiovascular Outcomes After an Acute Coronary Syndrome During Treatment With Alirocumab
Investigational drug: alirocumab
Document: Open-label therapy with alirocumab in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: Results from three years of treatment (journal, published 2016-11-09, source pmid:27886619)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Open-label therapy with alirocumab in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: Results from three years of treatment

BACKGROUND: PCSK9 inhibition with alirocumab significantly reduced LDL-C levels in trials of up to 78weeks' duration in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH). We report results from 3years of an ongoing open-label treatment extension (NCT01576484) to a 12-week double-blind trial in HeFH patients (NCT01266876). METHODS: Patients who completed the parent study and were receiving stable daily statin±ezetimibe could enter the open-label extension, where they received alirocumab 150mg every 2 weeks (Q2W) subcutaneously (n=58). The primary endpoint was safety (treatment-emergent adverse events, TEAEs). Efficacy endpoints included the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline at Week 24. Safety and efficacy data were available up to Weeks 156 and 148, respectively. RESULTS: Mean baseline LDL-C was 150.7mg/dL (3.9mmol/L), despite all patients being on a statin (76% on high-intensity statin; 72% also receiving ezetimibe). Over 156weeks, 54 (93.1%) patients experienced a TEAE, 12 (20.7%) experienced a serious TEAE, and two (3.4%) discontinued due to a TEAE. Injection site reactions occurred in 21 (36.2%) patients. Mean (SD) reduction in LDL-C from baseline to Week 24 was 65.4 (21.1)%, with reductions maintained through 148weeks (Week 148 reduction: 56.0 [23.8]%). Mean apolipoprotein B reduction was 50.9% and median lipoprotein (a) reduction was 22.5% at Week 24 (46.1% and 25.6% at Week 148, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Open-label treatment for 3years with alirocumab 150mg Q2W, administered with background statin±ezetimibe, was generally well-tolerated and had a safety profile comparable with that seen in the overall alirocumab clinical trial program. Alirocumab provided significant, sustained LDL-C reductions.
--- END ---
